requirements.quote: The DUP flag MUST be set to 1 by the Client or Server when it attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet [MQTT-3.3.1.-1].
requirements.condition: When a Client attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the DUP flag to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: A Client retransmission can be captured and its DUP bit inspected.

requirements.quote: The DUP flag MUST be set to 1 by the Client or Server when it attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet [MQTT-3.3.1.-1].
requirements.condition: When a Server attempts to re-deliver a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the DUP flag to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: A Server retransmission can be captured and its DUP bit inspected.

requirements.quote: The DUP flag MUST be set to 0 for all QoS 0 messages [MQTT-3.3.1-2].
requirements.condition: When sending a PUBLISH Packet with QoS 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the DUP flag to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The DUP bit of each emitted QoS 0 PUBLISH can be inspected.

requirements.quote: The value of the DUP flag from an incoming PUBLISH packet is not propagated when the PUBLISH Packet is sent to subscribers by the Server.
requirements.condition: When a Server sends an incoming PUBLISH Packet onward to subscribers.
requirements.required_behavior: Determine a new outgoing DUP value independently.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Propagate the incoming PUBLISH Packet's DUP value as the outgoing DUP value.
requirements.why_checkable: Incoming and outgoing DUP values can be compared while independently controlling whether the outgoing packet is a retransmission.

requirements.quote: The DUP flag in the outgoing PUBLISH packet is set independently to the incoming PUBLISH packet, its value MUST be determined solely by whether the outgoing PUBLISH packet is a retransmission [MQTT-3.3.1-3].
requirements.condition: When a Server sends a PUBLISH Packet to a subscriber and that outgoing packet is not a retransmission.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the outgoing DUP flag to 0, independently of the incoming PUBLISH Packet's DUP flag.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Use any fact other than outgoing retransmission status to choose the DUP value.
requirements.why_checkable: Fresh outgoing transmissions can be generated from incoming packets with either DUP value and must still carry DUP 0.

requirements.quote: The recipient of a Control Packet that contains the DUP flag set to 1 cannot assume that it has seen an earlier copy of this packet.
requirements.condition: When a recipient receives a Control Packet whose DUP flag is 1 without having observed an earlier copy.
requirements.required_behavior: Handle the packet without requiring a previously observed copy.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Assume that an earlier copy was necessarily received or reject the packet solely because no earlier copy is known.
requirements.why_checkable: A DUP 1 packet can be supplied as the first observed copy and receiver behavior can be tested.

requirements.quote: It is important to note that the DUP flag refers to the Control Packet itself and not to the Application Message that it contains.
requirements.condition: When interpreting a PUBLISH Packet's DUP flag.
requirements.required_behavior: Apply the duplicate indication to the Control Packet instance.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Treat the DUP flag as an indication that the contained Application Message itself is necessarily a duplicate.
requirements.why_checkable: Repeated Application Message content can be carried in distinct packet exchanges to test whether DUP is scoped to packets rather than payload identity.

requirements.quote: When using QoS 1, it is possible for a Client to receive a PUBLISH Packet with DUP flag set to 0 that contains a repetition of an Application Message that it received earlier, but with a different Packet Identifier.
requirements.condition: When a Client receives a QoS 1 PUBLISH with DUP 0 whose Application Message repeats earlier content but whose Packet Identifier is different.
requirements.required_behavior: Handle the PUBLISH as a distinct packet exchange rather than relying on Application Message equality to identify a retransmission.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Discard the packet solely because its Application Message content was received earlier.
requirements.why_checkable: Two QoS 1 packets with equal payloads, different identifiers, and DUP 0 can be injected and processing can be observed.

requirements.quote: Position: byte 1, bits 2-1.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the QoS field of a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the two-bit QoS field in bits 2 and 1 of byte 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The first PUBLISH header byte can be masked to verify the field position.

requirements.quote: 0	0	0	At most once delivery
requirements.condition: When encoding QoS value 0 in a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set QoS bit 2 to 0 and QoS bit 1 to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The two QoS bits can be compared with the table's exact 00 mapping.

requirements.quote: 0	0	0	At most once delivery
requirements.condition: When delivering an Application Message at QoS 0.
requirements.required_behavior: Provide at-most-once delivery.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Deliver the same QoS 0 publication more than once.
requirements.why_checkable: Delivery observations for a single QoS 0 publication can be counted to detect duplicates.

requirements.quote: 1	0	1	At least once delivery
requirements.condition: When encoding QoS value 1 in a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set QoS bit 2 to 0 and QoS bit 1 to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The two QoS bits can be compared with the table's exact 01 mapping.

requirements.quote: 1	0	1	At least once delivery
requirements.condition: When an Application Message is successfully delivered at QoS 1 under the protocol flow.
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver the publication at least once, allowing duplicates.
requirements.why_checkable: A completed QoS 1 exchange can be observed to verify that at least one delivery occurs while retransmission tests permit duplicates.

requirements.quote: 2	1	0	Exactly once delivery
requirements.condition: When encoding QoS value 2 in a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set QoS bit 2 to 1 and QoS bit 1 to 0.
requirements.why_checkable: The two QoS bits can be compared with the table's exact 10 mapping.

requirements.quote: 2	1	0	Exactly once delivery
requirements.condition: When an Application Message is successfully delivered at QoS 2 under the protocol flow.
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver the publication exactly once.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Deliver the same QoS 2 publication more than once.
requirements.why_checkable: A completed QoS 2 exchange, including retransmissions, can be observed and its application deliveries counted.

requirements.quote: A PUBLISH Packet MUST NOT have both QoS bits set to 1.
requirements.condition: When encoding a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Set QoS bit 2 and QoS bit 1 both to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The two QoS bits in an emitted PUBLISH header can be inspected for the reserved 11 combination.

requirements.quote: If a Server or Client receives a PUBLISH Packet which has both QoS bits set to 1 it MUST close the Network Connection [MQTT-3.3.1-4].
requirements.condition: When a Server or Client receives a PUBLISH Packet with QoS bits 2 and 1 both set to 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Close the Network Connection on which the invalid PUBLISH was received.
requirements.error_behavior: Terminate the Network Connection instead of continuing to process traffic on it.
requirements.why_checkable: A PUBLISH with the 11 QoS combination can be injected and connection closure observed.

requirements.quote: Position: byte 1, bit 0.
requirements.condition: When encoding or decoding the RETAIN flag of a PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Place the RETAIN flag in bit 0 of byte 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The first PUBLISH header byte can be masked to verify the flag position.

requirements.quote: If the RETAIN flag is set to 1, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST store the Application Message and its QoS, so that it can be delivered to future subscribers whose subscriptions match its topic name [MQTT-3.3.1-5].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives from a Client a QoS 1 or QoS 2 PUBLISH Packet whose RETAIN flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Store the Application Message for retained delivery on its topic.
requirements.why_checkable: Server retained state can be inspected or exercised through a later matching subscription.

requirements.quote: If the RETAIN flag is set to 1, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST store the Application Message and its QoS, so that it can be delivered to future subscribers whose subscriptions match its topic name [MQTT-3.3.1-5].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives from a Client a QoS 1 or QoS 2 PUBLISH Packet whose RETAIN flag is 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Store the Application Message's QoS as part of the retained state.
requirements.why_checkable: A future matching subscription can verify that retained delivery uses the stored QoS information.

requirements.quote: When a new subscription is established, the last retained message, if any, on each matching topic name MUST be sent to the subscriber [MQTT-3.3.1-6].
requirements.condition: When a new subscription is established and a matching topic has a retained message.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the last retained message on each matching topic name to the subscriber.
requirements.why_checkable: Preloaded retained messages and a new matching subscription can verify delivery for every matching topic.

requirements.quote: If the Server receives a QoS 0 message with the RETAIN flag set to 1 it MUST discard any message previously retained for that topic.
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a QoS 0 PUBLISH with RETAIN 1 for a topic that already has a retained message.
requirements.required_behavior: Discard the message previously retained for that topic.
requirements.why_checkable: A previous retained value can be installed, replaced by a QoS 0 retained publication, and queried through a later subscription.

requirements.quote: It SHOULD store the new QoS 0 message as the new retained message for that topic, but MAY choose to discard it at any time - if this happens there will be no retained message for that topic [MQTT-3.3.1-7].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a new QoS 0 PUBLISH with RETAIN 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Store the new QoS 0 message as the retained message for that topic.
requirements.why_checkable: The same sentence permits the Server to discard the message at any time, so observing absent retained state cannot deterministically establish noncompliance.

requirements.quote: It SHOULD store the new QoS 0 message as the new retained message for that topic, but MAY choose to discard it at any time - if this happens there will be no retained message for that topic [MQTT-3.3.1-7].
requirements.condition: If the Server exercises its permission to discard the new QoS 0 retained message.
requirements.required_behavior: Leave no retained message for that topic.
requirements.why_checkable: A subsequent new matching subscription can verify that no retained message is delivered for the topic after the discard.

requirements.quote: When sending a PUBLISH Packet to a Client the Server MUST set the RETAIN flag to 1 if a message is sent as a result of a new subscription being made by a Client [MQTT-3.3.1-8].
requirements.condition: When a Server sends a retained PUBLISH to a Client as a result of that Client making a new subscription.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the outgoing PUBLISH RETAIN flag to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: A new subscription can trigger retained delivery and the outgoing RETAIN bit can be inspected.

requirements.quote: It MUST set the RETAIN flag to 0 when a PUBLISH Packet is sent to a Client because it matches an established subscription regardless of how the flag was set in the message it received [MQTT-3.3.1-9].
requirements.condition: When a Server sends a PUBLISH to a Client because it matches an already established subscription.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the outgoing PUBLISH RETAIN flag to 0 regardless of the received message's RETAIN value.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Propagate a received RETAIN value of 1 onto this established-subscription delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: Messages with either incoming RETAIN value can be delivered through an established subscription and the outgoing flag inspected.

requirements.quote: A PUBLISH Packet with a RETAIN flag set to 1 and a payload containing zero bytes will be processed as normal by the Server and sent to Clients with a subscription matching the topic name.
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a PUBLISH with RETAIN 1 and a zero-byte payload while Clients have matching established subscriptions.
requirements.required_behavior: Send the zero-byte PUBLISH to the Clients whose subscriptions match the topic name.
requirements.why_checkable: Matching subscribers can be installed before injecting the zero-byte retained publication and deliveries can be observed.

requirements.quote: Additionally any existing retained message with the same topic name MUST be removed and any future subscribers for the topic will not receive a retained message [MQTT-3.3.1-10].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives a PUBLISH with RETAIN 1 and a zero-byte payload for a topic with an existing retained message.
requirements.required_behavior: Remove the existing retained message for that topic name.
requirements.why_checkable: Existing retained state can be installed and its removal verified after the zero-byte retained publication.

requirements.quote: Additionally any existing retained message with the same topic name MUST be removed and any future subscribers for the topic will not receive a retained message [MQTT-3.3.1-10].
requirements.condition: After a Server receives a PUBLISH with RETAIN 1 and a zero-byte payload for a topic.
requirements.required_behavior: Do not send a retained message for that topic to future subscribers.
requirements.why_checkable: A new matching subscription established afterward can be observed for absence of retained delivery.

requirements.quote: “As normal” means that the RETAIN flag is not set in the message received by existing Clients.
requirements.condition: When existing matching subscribers receive a zero-byte PUBLISH that arrived at the Server with RETAIN 1.
requirements.required_behavior: Set the outgoing RETAIN flag to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Send the packet to existing Clients with RETAIN set to 1.
requirements.why_checkable: The outgoing PUBLISH delivered to an existing subscriber can be captured and its RETAIN bit inspected.

requirements.quote: A zero byte retained message MUST NOT be stored as a retained message on the Server [MQTT-3.3.1-11].
requirements.condition: When a Server processes a retained PUBLISH whose payload contains zero bytes.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Store the zero-byte message as retained state.
requirements.why_checkable: A later new matching subscription can verify that the zero-byte message was not retained.

requirements.quote: If the RETAIN flag is 0, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST NOT store the message and MUST NOT remove or replace any existing retained message [MQTT-3.3.1-12].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives from a Client a PUBLISH Packet whose RETAIN flag is 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Store the received Application Message as retained state.
requirements.why_checkable: A later new matching subscription can verify that the RETAIN 0 message was not stored.

requirements.quote: If the RETAIN flag is 0, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST NOT store the message and MUST NOT remove or replace any existing retained message [MQTT-3.3.1-12].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives from a Client a PUBLISH Packet whose RETAIN flag is 0 and retained state already exists for the topic.
requirements.why_checkable: Previously installed retained state can be queried after processing the RETAIN 0 publication to verify it remains present.

requirements.quote: If the RETAIN flag is 0, in a PUBLISH Packet sent by a Client to a Server, the Server MUST NOT store the message and MUST NOT remove or replace any existing retained message [MQTT-3.3.1-12].
requirements.condition: When a Server receives from a Client a PUBLISH Packet whose RETAIN flag is 0 and retained state already exists for the topic.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Replace the existing retained message with the received message.
requirements.why_checkable: The retained value can be read through a later subscription and compared with the value stored before the RETAIN 0 publication.

requirements.quote: This is the length of variable header plus the length of the payload.
requirements.condition: When calculating the Remaining Length field of this PUBLISH Packet.
requirements.required_behavior: Set Remaining Length to the variable-header byte length plus the payload byte length.
requirements.why_checkable: The declared Remaining Length can be compared with the measured sizes of the variable header and payload.
